| Servings = 4–6

{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|Cuisine of France]] | [[Cookbook:Meat and Poultry|Meat]]

Many French regions claim '''coq au vin''', or chicken stew, as their own, but legend has it that the recipe originated with [[w:Julius Caesar|Caesar]]'s chef. Different variants exist throughout the world. Note that you can also use [[cookbook:capon|capon]].

== Ingredients ==
__NOTOC__
* 1.5 [[Cookbook:kg|kg]] (about 3.5 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]]) [[cookbook:chicken|chicken]], jointed (or drumsticks, thighs, breasts); get the giblets, and the blood if you can; season beforehand; marrow is important.
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], [[Cookbook:Chop|chopped]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ¼ tsp [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]]
* 200 [[Cookbook:g|g]] (about ¼ lb) small [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]]
* 240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]) [[Cookbook:Red Wine|red wine]]
* 1 clove [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]]
* 1 tsp [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] and fresh
* 1 tsp fresh or dried [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]]
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]] for sautéing

== Special equipment ==
* Wide [[cookbook:skillet|skillet]]
* Deep pyrex bowl with lid
* Jug

== Procedure ==
#Mix flour, salt and pepper. Coat chicken, onion and carrot in flour mixture and set aside.
#[[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] mushrooms, set aside.
#[[Cookbook:Browning|Brown]] the chicken pieces a few at a time, set aside.
#Brown onions and carrots. Put chicken into large [[Cookbook:Casserole (pot)|casserole]] on medium-high heat along with onions, carrots and mushrooms.
#Combine wine, garlic, and basil; pour over chicken.
#Cover the casserole, cook until chicken is ready (1–1.5 hours), stirring occasionally.

==External links==
*[http://www.observer.co.uk/life/story/0,6903,605460,00.html Perfect Coq au Vin] via ''The Observer''
